chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Taghlub, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the meat of horses, so he said: 'Do not eat it unless necessity befalls you.' And [I asked] about the meat of domesticated donkeys, so he said: 'In the Book of Ali (peace be upon him) it is recorded that he forbade eating it.'

key_terms.كِتَابِ عَلِيٍّ: Book of Ali (referring to a specific legal record or epistle)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating horse and donkey meat in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the distinct juristic status of horse and domesticated donkey meat, reflecting the Shia tradition of deriving rulings from both the Imams and the authoritative 'Book of Ali' (Kitab Ali). While horse meat is permitted generally but discouraged unless necessity dictates, the prohibition of domesticated donkey meat is rooted in the specific injunctions recorded in the Prophet’s or Imam’s written legacy, highlighting the interplay between oral transmission and textual authority in Shia fiqh.
